note:
ISO 2026-W22 runs from May 25 through May 31. Ceres and Uranus are separated by about 3.3° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌕 Full Moon · Flower Moon — 08:45:13 UTC. Bright moonlight favors prominent stars and planets while reducing contrast on faint deep-sky objects. Use Mizar, Spica as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -10.7; direct motion; 66.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude May 31 08:45 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -1.2; direct motion; 86.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 81.7% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.3; direct motion; 96.8% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: In solar glare; magnitude 8.7; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -1.9; direct motion; 99.5% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.9; direct motion; 99.8% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: In solar glare; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.5; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace Coma Berenices’s charted figure in the finder, then identify Diadem at its charted position. Trace Coma Berenices’s charted figure in the finder, then identify β Com at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** NGC 4945: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; MCG 6-29-52: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M53: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; MCG 6-29-62: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Sunflower Galaxy: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Centaurus A: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Omega Centauri: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Whirlpool Galaxy: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: Astronomical lunar phase near opposition to the Sun.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.

Why it is here: The Calendar selected Fixed object 301 as one of this week’s fixed-sky observing targets.

story_candidates.dek: Diadem is a star in Com of catalogue visual magnitude 4.32; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
The stored catalogue gives a visual magnitude of 4.32. This is a catalogue value, not a prediction of its brightness this week. Lower magnitudes mean brighter objects; sky brightness and altitude affect whether you can see the star.

Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 13h 09m and declination +17.5°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star rises and sets, reaching approximately 63° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Com constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
